title: Unit 3 : Session 9 : SLO 2 — Restoring Division (Simulation & Analysis)
sections: Section C: Paper Simulation (Apply): 0110 (6) ÷ 0010 (2) — restoring division
Restoration is triggered whenever the subtraction produces a negative remainder — the subtraction 'failed', so the divisor is added back to recover the previous remainder.
The division is complete after n cycles, where n is the number of bits of the quotient/dividend register; the quotient sits in Q and the remainder in A.
Each left shift brings the next dividend bit into the remainder for the trial subtraction and simultaneously frees the LSB of Q to receive the new quotient bit.
